title: Seaman
subtitle: A creature that answers back
summary: Seaman is Vivarium's virtual-pet simulation, first released for Dreamcast in Japan on 29 July 1999.
body: Seaman is Vivarium's virtual-pet simulation, first released for Dreamcast in Japan on 29 July 1999. The player cares for strange fish-like creatures with human faces, using a microphone accessory to speak to them. Food, suitable conditions and regular attention keep the inhabitants alive as they develop. Designer Yoot Saito makes the aquarium into a place for conversation as well as care. The creature gradually becomes a companion that responds, asks questions and comments on the person outside the screen, giving an ordinary television an unexpectedly uncomfortable inhabitant.

The simulation follows real time, requiring the player to return on subsequent days and check the creatures' condition. A long absence can have consequences, so progress depends on forming a small routine rather than completing a continuous sequence of levels. Speaking into the microphone supplies the company that Seaman needs. Questions may concern the player's birthday, allowing the creature to respond with events associated with that date. The exchange mixes personal details with trivia, making each visit feel like another conversation with an increasingly familiar resident.

Seaman's blunt remarks give the relationship a comic edge. Keeping a creature alive does not guarantee polite gratitude, and the contrast between its face, voice and aquarium body is central to the effect. The microphone plugs into the Dreamcast controller, turning a hardware accessory into the game's main point of contact. A Japanese PlayStation 2 adaptation followed later. The original remains distinctive for the way its limited daily actions build anticipation: returning means checking on a living thing that may have something new, and possibly unflattering, to say.
